newsitem.title: UK: BoE says pound won't cut inflation two years out.
newsitem.headline: BoE says pound won't cut inflation two years out.

text.p: The Bank of England on Tuesday admitted the strength of sterling had created a policy dilemma and would lead to a temporary fall in inflation but said it would not help meet Britain's 2.5 percent inflation target further out.

The Bank said the pound had created an increasing imbalance between growth in manufacturing and services but said it thought a significant part of sterling's rise was purely erratic and could be reversed more quickly than current interest rate differentials suggest.
The bank said the strength of sterling should push inflation, excluding mortgage interest repayments, well below the government's target of 2.5 percent this year.
But it said that this measure of inflation would more likely than not be above the government's target in two years' time despite sterling's rise.

Last week the new Labour government gave the Bank of England freedom to set interest rates. Analysts said the report showed the central bank was still concerned about inflationary pressures in the economy, growing at an annual rate of more than three percent.

David Coleman, economist at CIBC Wood Gundy, said: "The surprise is that they are still calling for another tightening of policy before seeing the effects of the last one." Sterling rose against the mark after the report's release.
